items.title: MedGauge: A Metrological Framework for Measuring Medical AI Agents by Program-Graded Work Products
items.abstract: Evaluation of medical AI has inherited its instruments from the evaluation of people: examinations, expert judgement of free text, and task value denominated in the hours a practitioner would need. This working paper asks which of those instruments survive when the thing measured is a silicon producer (a model running inside a harness with tools) and builds a measurement framework for the parts that do not. It is the argument for the construction of the MedGauge Methodology, version 0.1.0 (https://medgauge.org/methodology/text/), which is the normative text. It tests the claim that silicon producers differ from human producers against the literature and finds twelve properties of silicon producers that bear on measurement, each stated with its counter-evidence; a difference from people is supported for two of them by an opened source, three hold by construction of the subject, and for the remaining seven no source states the human side and no difference is asserted. It shows that human-anchored evaluations divide into anchors on human time (which transfer as a predictor of difficulty but not as a unit), on a human product or rule (which transfer once the product is converted into a key of field checks set independently by two experts) and on human judgement of free text or preference (which do not transfer). On that basis it builds the measurement: following the international vocabulary of metrology, the reference of each quantity moves from a unit to a versioned grading program applied to a fixed artifact contract. It gives scale rules for labels, levels and counts; proposes base and derived quantities with their scale type, traceability and cross-harness comparability; maps them onto ten measurement dimensions and ten task labels; and sets out an examination regime in which a subject passes only if every task passes in all three runs with no safety veto, the strength of a pass being a one-sided 95% lower bound on reliability, with execution errors counted as failures, paired comparison with step-down multiplicity control, and no overall score. Version 0.1.0 of the methodology sets no level threshold and issues no level. The paper proposes a four-layer task typology with its literature base, explains why a closed, uncalibrated, generated task set licenses an attribute-sampling regime but not a response-model regime, and sets out the uncertainty budget for the chain from a published score to its public source clause. Standardised semantics for products, scenarios and task types, and the validation of those standards, are set out as a research plan, not as results. The paper reports no measurement result. At the date of publication the public site is live, no benchmark round has been run, no result record exists and every leaderboard is empty.

items.title: Media education, digital literacy, and teacher education: pedagogical perspectives on the critical construction of meaning in digital contexts
items.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping the relationship between knowledge, education, and society, prompting pedagogy to reconsider the ways teaching and learning are understood. The educational challenge extends beyond the introduction of innovative technologies into schools and concerns the processes through which knowledge is produced, interpreted, or ganized, and shared. As highlighted by UNESCO (2023), artificial intelligence represents one of the major educational challenges of our time because it actively influences the construction of meaning and transforms the forms of cultural mediation traditionally performed by schools. Consequently, the central issue is not whether AI should be embraced or rejected, but how it can be integrated into pedagogical practices that foster critical thinking and digital citizenship. The evolution of digital environments demonstrates that access to information no longer guarantees knowledge construction. items.title: Medical School Curriculum Reform and the Missing Debate on Artificial Intelligence as an Educational Agent
items.abstract: In 2024, revision of the Enforcement Decree of the Higher Education Act in Korea abolished the rigid division between the 2-year premedical phase and the 4-year medical phase, allowing medical schools to design 6-year curricula autonomously for the first time in a century. Universities nationwide have begun redesigning their programs accordingly. This historic reform coincides with the rapid spread of generative artificial intelligence (AI) across society, including the ways students learn. In the current curriculum reform discourse, however, AI is discussed almost exclusively as content to be taught or as a supplementary tool to be used, whereas the more fundamental question of AI as an educational agent remains largely unexamined. Outside the formal curriculum, AI tutors already function as de facto teachers: a randomized experiment suggests that well-designed AI tutoring can outperform expert- led active-learning classrooms, and international surveys indicate that medical students routinely consult AI before, or instead of, their professors. This paper argues that the widening gap between the official, faculty-centered curriculum and the actual AI-mediated learning ecosystem may create discord: AI-mediated learning may become an unmanaged informal curriculum, faculty-designed assessment may lose authority, and trust in the formal curriculum may erode. Curriculum reform that merely rearranges the 6-year structure without addressing who teaches risks producing an elaborate design for an education that no longer reflects how learning occurs. Medical schools should explicitly define the position, scope, and governance of AI as an educational agent within their new curricula.

items.title: Meeting LLMs for the First Time: Understanding Trust Formation and Adjustment Among Older Adults in China
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid population aging and the proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) in China, this study investigates the dynamics of trust formation and adjustment among Chinese older adults during their initial encounters with LLM agents. Through in-depth interviews conducted before, during, and immediately after 30 older adults’ first interactions with six widely used Chinese LLM applications, followed by second interviews with 26 participants, the study examines how trust was initially formed and adjusted over the short term. Findings reveal that pre-interaction responses were predominantly characterized by low interest and skepticism, rooted in sociocultural perceptions rather than just technological barriers. Analysis identified four technological factors associated with participants’ trust-related judgments during engagement, including personalization, anthropomorphism, conversationality, and response latency. Longitudinal analysis identified three behavioral patterns of trust adjustment: Limited Correction, Collaborative Reciprocity, and Cognitive Entrenchment. These findings advance theoretical understanding of trust adjustment and calibration-related processes and offer design implications for building more trustworthy LLMs.

items.abstract: This study examines the theological significance of the doctrine of Imago Dei in response to the ethical challenges posed by artificial intelligence to human dignity and identity. Utilizing a qualitative literature review approach, the research analyzes how technological advancements in AI necessitate a profound reflection on theological anthropology. The findings indicate that the Imago Dei remains the foundational framework for affirming human uniqueness and dignity amidst digital progress. Consequently, AI development and utilization must be guided by Christian ethical principles to ensure technology supports human well-being without eroding core values. Ultimately, the study highlights the need for a contextual reconstruction of Christian spirituality and ethics, enabling believers to engage with AI wisely, responsibly, and in alignment with their divine calling as God's image.

items.title: Memory-Os: AI-Powered Personal Knowledge Operating System
items.abstract: Memory-OS is an AI-powered Personal Knowledge Operating System designed to unify personal and development-related information through a conversational command-line interface. The system integrates external knowledge sources such as GitHub, Gmail, and Notion through a connector-based architecture and processes collected information for efficient retrieval. It uses a local sentence-transformer model to generate embeddings, Qdrant for vector storage, Neo4j for knowledge graph relationships, and SQLite for structured data management. A hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline combines semantic search, keyword-based retrieval, and graph-based context to generate relevant and context-aware responses using a Groq-powered Large Language Model (LLM). Memory-OS also provides an interactive terminal interface, a full-screen Textual TUI, workspace management, incremental synchronization, Docker-based service provisioning, health diagnostics, backup and restore functionality, and performance monitoring. The primary objective is to reduce information fragmentation by enabling users to search, connect, and understand their accumulated knowledge through natural-language queries instead of manually navigating multiple applications.

items.title: Migrating a Legacy Scientific Application with an AI Coding Agent: NICAM from Fortran to Kokkos
items.abstract: Migrating from Fortran to C++/Kokkos broadens access to hardware accelerators through backends such as CUDA and HIP while offering greater flexibility in software design. However, legacy Fortran applications often have large codebases, making manual porting time-consuming and costly. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and AI coding agents have made large-scale code migration increasingly feasible. In this study, we ported NICAM (Nonhydrostatic ICosahedral Atmospheric Model), a legacy Fortran climate model accelerated with OpenACC, to C++/Kokkos with the assistance of Claude Code. The agent translated the code directly from Fortran to C++/Kokkos under human review. Approximately 140,000 lines of Fortran were analyzed and ported into 35,000 lines of C++/Kokkos, covering the dynamical core and seven physics packages. A 100-member ensemble comparison with the original Fortran model showed that the port is statistically consistent with the original. Performance was evaluated on Miyabi-G, an NVIDIA GH200 cluster, and Sirius, an AMD MI300A cluster. Compared with the Fortran/OpenACC baseline on GH200, the port achieved application speedups of $1.71\times$ on GH200 and $1.54\times$ on MI300A. The CUDA build achieved a GPU kernel-time speedup of $1.38\times$ on GH200. After normalization by peak memory bandwidth, the HIP build on MI300A achieved $0.96\times$ the kernel performance of the Fortran/OpenACC baseline.

items.title: Mirror neurons and artificial intelligence: educational pathways for socio-emotional inclusion in technology-mediated learning environments
items.abstract: This contribution analyses the relationship between mirror neurons, Artificial Intelligence, Affective Computing, and educational technologies for the socio-emotional inclusion of students with ASD. Social robots, augmented reality, and intelligent systems are understood as pedagogical mediators, capable of making social cues more accessible and fostering personalised learning environments. The mirror neuron system offers a key framework for understanding the embodied nature of intersubjectivity. The sharing of neural codes between observed and executed actions allows imitation, empathy, and the understanding of others to be interpreted as processes integrating perception, action, and emotion (Gallese, 2008). Learning is thus a relational, situated experience. This framework dialogues with AI architectures. Artificial neural networks learn from data and generalise responses, but their pedagogical value depends on supporting adaptive interactions. Social robots, immersive environments, and augmented reality may offer structured contexts in which students exercise communicative and socio-emotional skills through feedback and recognisable routines. items.title: Modern Methods of Preserving Meat and Meat Products: A Comprehensive Literature Review
items.abstract: In the face of growing consumer demands, tightening legal regulations, and the global problem of food waste, the meat industry is undergoing a dynamic transformation. Traditional, synthetic additive-based preservation methods are being replaced by innovative, integrated technologies. This review article analyzes the latest scientific reports (from 2016–2026) indexed in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect databases regarding modern methods of meat and meat product preservation. The mechanisms of action and the impact of advanced non-thermal technologies, such as high hydrostatic pressure (HPP), high-intensity ultrasound (HIU), atmospheric pressure cold plasma (ACP), pulsed light (PL), and rotating and oscillating magnetic fields (RMF/OMF), are discussed in detail. The role of biopreservation in the context of the “clean label” trend was also presented, including the use of lactic acid bacteria, bacteriocins, bacteriophages, and nanoencapsulated plant extracts. Furthermore, innovations in materials engineering were analyzed—active packaging releasing antimicrobial substances and intelligent freshness indicators based on natural halochrome dyes. The whole is complemented by an analysis of the impact of Industry 4.0 solutions, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), hyperspectral imaging (HSI), and the Internet of Things (IoT), on cold chain optimization and digital quality management.

items.title: MONITORING THE REHABILITATION PROCESS USING A SMART ELECTRONIC TOOL FOR IMPLEMENTING THE PUSH & RELEASE TEST
items.abstract: Introduction. The modernization of monitoring procedures is recognized as critical to improving the objectivity and effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions in the physical education of students with disabilities. The purpose of the study was to develop and conduct experimental and metrological testing of smart electronic system for monitoring the rehabilitation process of students with disabilities following blast-induced traumatic brain injury. Materials and Methods. The study was conducted in three consecutive stages: theoretical justification; the development of a smart electronic system pedagogical experiment and data processing using mathematical statistics methods. The study involved first-year students (28 males) with disabilities following a blast traumatic brain injury, who were enrolled in a physical education course lasting one academic semester. The Push & Release Test was used to collect empirical data. Results. The study aims to develop an intelligent electronic system for the objective monitoring of the P&R Test, particularly those parameters that cannot be recorded visually. An intelligent electronic system has been developed and tested, consisting of a sensor module (a smart IMU sensor based on a microcontroller, accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer), an impact force and alignment measurement module (a strain gauge platform with four high-precision strain sensors), an intelligent data processing unit with an Arduino microcontroller, and a personal computer with real-time wireless signal transmission. The system’s functional components were modeled in Python using artificial intelligence algorithms to automate the analysis and prediction of students’ functional status from test results. The implementation of neural network-based artificial intelligence algorithms enabled the automatic classification of movement patterns and the highly accurate prediction of students’ functional status following a mild traumatic brain injury. A virtual reality interface is integrated into the system, creating a «virtual mirror» effect for interactive feedback. Empirical and metrological validation of the system confirmed its high reliability (ICC – 0.844) and validity (ICC – 0.521) compared to traditional expert assessment reliability (ICC – 0.506) and validity (ICC – 0.188) by an examiner. Conclusions. The developed digital system provides examiners with qualitative and quantitative data, minimizes the «human factor», and significantly improves the effectiveness of monitoring the rehabilitation process of students with blast TBI during a university physical education course.

items.title: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos
items.abstract: Scaling humanoid motion foundation models is constrained by the scarcity of diverse, robot-executable data and by the difficulty of jointly learning from heterogeneous multimodal inputs while supporting real-time closed-loop control. We present Movens-5M, constructed from raw Internet videos through clip generation, quality filtering, semantic annotation, motion recovery, and physical refinement with humanoid retargeting and execution verification. It contains 15 million human-motion sequences and 5 million physically executable humanoid-motion sequences spanning over 10,000 hours, aligned with text, RGB video, speech, and music. Building on this data, we introduce Movens-Zero, a scalable understanding-generation-execution architecture that supports joint learning across modalities and real-time closed-loop execution. Task-mixed flow-matching training jointly optimizes a single action expert across seven generation tasks, enabling direct motion generation from text, speech, music, and video. Multimodal Real-Time Chunking connects overlapping chunks under continuously updated instructions and robot states for continuous closed-loop execution. We further introduce Movens-Intent, a four-track benchmark with 8,192 expert-verified condition-motion pairs across text, speech, music, and video. Experiments show consistent gains across all four modalities when scaling execution-verified data from 1% to 100% and action-expert capacity from 64M to 911M parameters, while demonstrating that data quality and cross-modal supervision improve generation and execution.

items.title: MULTI-TIERED MEDICATION RECONCILIATION AND SAFETY PROTOCOLS IN HIGH-VOLUME EMERGENCY ENVIRONMENTS: MITIGATING IATROGENIC RISK THROUGH ALGORITHMIC DECISION SUPPORT AND INTERPROFESSIONAL GOVERNANCE
items.abstract: Background: Medication use in emergency departments (EDs) occurs under time pressure, incomplete histories, frequent transitions, interruptions, and rapidly changing clinical conditions. These features create risk at prescribing, reconciliation, dispensing, administration, monitoring, and handover. A single intervention cannot control all failure modes. Aim: To develop a multi-tiered medication safety protocol that integrates closed-loop barcode verification, clinical pharmacist triage consultation, adverse event mitigation, and interprofessional systems governance. Methods: A focused evidence synthesis was combined with a descriptive secondary analysis of published aggregate findings. Evidence was extracted from patient-safety sources and peer-reviewed reports addressing ED medication-error prevalence, barcode medication administration (BCMA), adverse drug events, clinical-pharmacy functions, and governance. No simulated or patient-level data were used. Results: A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis summarized through AHRQ PSNet reported a pooled ED medication-error prevalence of 22% and estimated that 36% of patients experienced a medication error; approximately 43% of those errors were potentially harmful without leading to death. A single Veterans Affairs ED study reported an almost 11% reduction in medication-error rates after BCMA implementation, while also identifying unsafe workarounds. The evidence supports layered controls rather than technology alone. Conclusion: Safe emergency medication use requires a sociotechnical system. Barcode verification should be embedded within reliable patient identification, pharmacist triage, interruption control, high-alert safeguards, event mitigation, learning systems, and shared governance. The proposed protocol provides an operational framework for implementation, auditing, and continuous improvement.

items.title: Multilingualism and Multisensory Technologies: Towards Inclusive Digital Language Learning
items.abstract: The growing prevalence of digital technologies and the increasing linguistic diversity of contemporary societies are profoundly changing the processes of language teaching and learning (Piccardo, 2019). Against this backdrop, multilingualism and multisensory technologies represent two closely interlinked dimensions, capable of contributing to the creation of educational environments that are more inclusive, participatory and geared towards the development of language skills (Kress, 2021). This paper presents a review of the international literature with the aim of analysing the relationship between multilingualism and digital technologies, with particular reference to immersive environments, artificial intelligence systems and Digital Language Learning Ecosystems (PintoLlorente & Alvarez, 2024). The analysis takes into account theoretical studies, meta -analyses and systematic reviews published in recent years, linking the main findings of research on language learning with the latest technological innovations. items.title: Multimodal In-Context Learning with Explicit Rule Induction
items.abstract: A central challenge in multimodal in-context learning (MICL) arises from tasks that are ill-defined without context and require uncovering the underlying rules from demonstrations. Existing methods predominantly treat MICL as direct input-output mapping, overlooking the importance of explicitly inducing and reasoning over such rules, limiting both performance and interpretability. We propose ERIM, Explicit Rule-Induction for Multimodal In-Context Learning, a unified framework that enhances MICL by explicitly inducing the latent rules governing demonstration samples. Leveraging the reasoning ability of multi-modal large language model (MLLM), ERIM constructs rule-centric MICL datasets, introduces explicit supervision for rule induction, and fine-tunes MLLM to perform explicit rule-induction via a two-stage training strategy that combines mixed cold-start supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments show consistent performance improvements across diverse MICL settings and demonstrate that correctly inducing underlying rules directly leads to stronger and more stable performance.

items.title: Multimodal Large Language Model-Enabled Healthcare Information System Design
items.abstract: Cross-border health-care information systems often struggle to deliver culturally embedded medical knowledge—such as traditional Chinese medicine—to international users with varying health literacy, due to fragmented architecture and weak semantic alignment across languages. This study proposed a tripartite framework built on the Qwen2.5 Vision-Language model at the 7-billion parameter scale, integrating cross-lingual perception, domain knowledge enhancement, and terminology alignment to support multimodal health-care information processing. A bidirectional label-matching feedback mechanism and an entropy-weighted coupling coordination model were developed to quantify system-level synergy. Using 12,642 dissemination records and 7,869 health-care cases (2019–2025), the proposed system outperformed OpenAI's generative pretrained transformer 4o mini by 7.1 points on average across core indicators, with coupling coordination rising from 0.409 to 0.716 and regional synergy gains of 0.382 in Southeast Asia. The framework achieved a 39.2% retention rate in full-chain service conversion and over 83% adaptability for low-health-literacy users.

items.title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
items.abstract: Self-distillation methods for large language models with an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher already retain a history of student updates. Muon nevertheless stores a separate momentum buffer, increasing persistent training memory. We propose Muon with Reused Teacher (Muon-RT), which reuses the teacher-student displacement to eliminate momentum buffers for hidden weight matrices. We show that this displacement encodes an exponentially weighted history of applied updates and smooths temporally uncorrelated noise under a local model. Muon-RT removes its radial component, normalizes it spectrally, and mixes it with the current gradient after Newton-Schulz (NS) orthogonalization. Under explicit regularity and alignment assumptions, we establish linear contraction of an expected objective-gap bound toward a residual error level. With Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Muon-RT improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.6 points with 42% less persistent memory, and over momentum Muon by 5.4 points with 27% less persistent memory. With Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO) on Olmo-3-7B-Instruct, it improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.0 points.

items.title: Musculoskeletal neck pain in patients with migraine: pathophysiological relationship, diagnosis and treatment
items.abstract: Musculoskeletal neck pain (NP) is more common in people with headaches (HA) than in those without HA. NP is most frequently associated with primary forms of HA. In real-world clinical practice, patients with NP and concomitant HA are often misdiagnosed, with HA being regarded as secondary and associated with organic pathology of the cervical spine. Consequently, such patients often do not receive effective treatment, or the treatment provided has only a temporary effect. We present the case of a female patient with migraine and NP. A combined approach was used to treat the patient, comprising a course of a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (Nimesil) and non-pharmacological therapy – educational discussions with the patient about the condition, individual kinesiotherapy sessions, kinesiotaping, training in ergonomic principles and correct posture, and physical activity in daily life. After 2 months of treatment, the patient’s musculoskeletal pain and headaches associated with cervical myofascial pain syndrome had resolved; only rare migraine attacks remained, which were effectively relieved by a triptan. Follow-up of the patient over a 12-month period demonstrated the sustainability of the clinical improvement achieved, confirming the effectiveness of the described therapeutic approach in the treatment of musculoskeletal neck pain and associated migraine.

items.title: Natural Dopamine: Nature’s Seven DIURNAL Environmental Enrichment Properties in Changing Visual Complexity
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Time spent in unchanging environments is associated with poorer brain, cognitive and mental health outcomes, while environmental enrichment for humans is measured by how much nature is present rather than how it changes. Methods: This study quantified nature’s changing visual complexity using a large-language-model scoring method validated against a deep-learning complexity metric previously tested using event-related potentials. Photos were taken of a natural scene, a tree, and the sky across minutes, days, and seasons (1115 photographs; 2024 to 2026). Results: The analysis identified seven quantitative properties describing nature’s dynamic environmental enrichment in changing visual complexity: Dichotomy, Inclination, Unpredictability, Renewal, Net balance, Amplitude, and Level (DIURNAL). A quantitative simulation then showed that a natural view offers more change than indoor and urban views, consistent with the argument that unchanging environments are detrimental to the brain, which is hypothesised here to act through a dopaminergic pathway. Conclusions: DIURNAL raises questions for biophilic design and for how neurotypical and neurodivergent brains respond to change in visual complexity in nature, digital environments and built environments.

items.title: Neck pain in office workers
items.abstract: Office workers are at risk of developing neck pain (NP), which is one of the main causes of temporary incapacity for work and disability. NP associated with office work is caused by a combination of individual, physical and psychosocial factors. Identifying the factors that predispose office workers to the development and chronicity of NP may contribute to the primary and secondary prevention of pain. A multisystem approach to the treatment and prevention of NP among office workers is recognized as the most effective; it includes optimization of the work-place in accordance with ergonomic principles, therapeutic exercises and psychological intervention. The drugs of choice for relieving NP are nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, among which aceclofenac (Aertal) is one of the most effective and safe.

items.title: Needs and barriers of healthcare teams to implement real-time AI & predictive analytics in cardiothoracic ICU: a field study
items.abstract: Introduction Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers significant opportunities to improve healthcare quality, especially in critical care settings, where timely decisions are essential yet challenging due to the volume of continuously accumulating patient data. AI algorithms can analyze data in real time, summarize key information for busy care teams, and alert clinicians to critical events and important care milestones. However, successful implementation requires first understanding the needs and barriers care teams face, including needs that are currently missing from their workflow, and what obstacles to integration exist. Methods To address these questions, we conducted a field study in a Cardiothoracic Intensive Care Unit (CT-ICU) to evaluate user needs for implementing real-time AI predictive analytics. We observed and interviewed fourteen participants ( n = 14), including nursing staff, advanced practice providers (NP/PAs), cardiovascular critical care attending physicians, and surgeons. Through a qualitative thematic analysis, we identified key considerations for developing and implementing static and real-time AI and predictive tools in the CT-ICU, aligning with the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) constructs of perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use . Findings Key themes included: (1) the system must have added clinical value to the clinical team and patients, (2) trust in the AI system should be prioritized through co-design processes, transparency in the system, and consistent prediction accuracy, and (3) integration into workflow was critical, including robust onboarding and minimizing alarm fatigue, charting burden, click burden, and technology burden with consideration of personal wellness. Conclusion As a synthesis of our findings, we identify a series of key design insights and suggest a preliminary framework for AI technology development focused on clinical team trust and adoption, the Trusted AI for Clinical Teams (TACT) framework. These findings offer the potential to bridge from AI research to clinical implementation.

items.title: Negative affectivity moderates the association between job demands and hair cortisol in healthcare workers: a cross-sectional multi-method study
items.abstract: Aims Healthcare workers (HCWs) are frequently exposed to psychosocial job demands (JDs) that may lead to work-related stress. This study investigates the association between JDs—specifically time pressure, problem solving, overload, and emotional demands—and hair cortisol concentration (HCC), as biomarker of long-term hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis activation, in a sample of HCWs. It further examines the moderating role of negative affectivity (NA), an individual characteristic linked to heightened stress reactivity. Drawing on the Job Demands–Resources theory and the allostatic load model, we hypothesized that (1) JDs would be positively associated with HCC and (2) this relationship would be stronger for individuals high in NA. Design Participants were 67 healthcare professionals working in a healthcare facility located in Northern Italy. Participants completed a self-report questionnaire designed to assess JDs and NA. Next, participants provided a hair sample for the assessment of HCC. Results Although data from a sample of HCWs revealed some positive but non-significant trends for problem solving and overload, generally JDs were not associated with HCC at average levels of NA. Interestingly, NA moderated the relationship between problem solving/time pressure and HCC, with stronger positive associations among individuals with high NA. Conclusion Findings from this exploratory cross-sectional study suggest that NA may act as a vulnerability factor, implying that HCWs high in NA may have a heightened strain response to certain JDs. By integrating psychological and biological measures, this study offers novel insights into the interplay between workplace stressors, personality traits, and physiological responses to stress. These findings highlight the potential relevance of individual differences in occupational stress research, and point to HCC as a promising indicator of chronic stress among HCWs. Implications for the profession The findings suggest the need for occupational health interventions tailored to individual traits, such as NA, to reduce stress reactivity, foster well-being, and enhance the quality of care provided.

items.title: Neuro-symbolic AI for proactive risk forecasting: bridging large language models and dynamic Bayesian networks
items.abstract: Purpose Periodic risk reports constitute a substantial repository of operational data for project management. Despite the inherent informational value, archived records remain largely unstructured and highly fragmented. This study proposes a fully local neuro-symbolic approach for dynamic risk forecasting by translating qualitative project narratives into a quantifiable predictive engine to support decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The proposed methodology adopts a mixed-methods architecture including four layers: (1) spatial morphology reconstruction using a Y-axis density clustering algorithm; (2) a hybrid pseudonymization filter; (3) a local large language model (LLM) with chain-of-thought reasoning; and (4) a symbolic causal engine powered by a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to quantify causal propagation into a dynamic risk index. Findings An empirical evaluation across 28 reporting cycles spanning a 33-month large-scale infrastructure project indicates that the symbolic layer provides a temporally coherent aggregation of the output of a zero-shot perception layer operating at a macro F1-score of 53.62%. By quantifying causal risk propagation, the DBN captured a 93.59% risk-saturation state, for which the retrieved evidence identifies chronic site-clearance bottlenecks. Notably, using an alert threshold selected by sensitivity analysis together with an analytic constraint on the posterior mass attributable to the critical state (talert = 70.0%), the model outputs Bayesian probabilities alongside LLM-extracted textual evidence, yielding an anticipation interval of 1.33 reporting cycles relative to the documented administrative response. Originality/value The neuro-symbolic framework bridges the gap between deep learning perception and causal inference in construction management. By coupling LLM-driven zero-shot ordinal extraction with DBN causal reasoning, the research establishes an auditable framework for risk documentation. The integrated framework transitions AI from an opaque prediction model into an accountable decision-support tool, providing stakeholders with transparent explainable AI diagnostics and supporting a shift from reactive mitigation to proactive, evidence-based risk prevention.

items.title: New prediction model for school dropout based on an improvement of SVM and ABC optimization algorithm
items.abstract: School dropout is a major dare for Moroccan education systems. It generates profound repercussions, both socially and economically, affecting both individuals and the entire community. To assess the risks associated with this phenomenon, it is essential to use innovative technologies, relying in particular on statistical methods and artificial intelligence models capable of providing effective results using available data. These methods offer the possibility of identifying the factors influencing the educational phenomenon and anticipating the associated risks. To understand the effect of scholars’ social, economic, and personal influences on school dropout, we propose in this work a new classifier, based on an improvement of support vector machines (SVM) and on the ABC algorithm. We also present a regression model designed to estimate academic performance based on the average grade obtained. We also propose a new regression model to predict the degree of academic achievement. The proposed model was validated on a real dataset, compiled from a questionnaire distributed to Moroccan secondary school students. Furthermore, several comparative studies were conducted with recent approaches to assess the performance of the proposed methods. All the experimental results confirm the robustness and improved performance of the developed methods, particularly with respect to accuracy and predictive capability.

items.title: Next-Generation Library Services Using AI and Big Data
items.abstract: Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Big Data, academic libraries are evolving from traditional repositories into state-of-the-art, user-centric knowledge and research hubs. This chapter highlights key applications of AI and Big Data in academic libraries and explores the conceptual evolution of library services from Library 1.0 to Library 4.0. Technologies such as chatbots and virtual reference services, personalised recommendations, automated cataloguing and metadata generation, intelligent search capabilities, and research and learning analytics are all enabled by AI. Through Big Data analytics, libraries can better understand user behaviour, enhance collection development, maximise resource utilisation, and facilitate datadriven and predictive decision-making. Emerging technologies like blockchain, cloud computing, robotics, and the Internet of Things further support the development of smart library infrastructure. In India, technology-enabled library services are being facilitated by initiatives such as the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the National Digital Library of India (NDLI), e-ShodhSindhu, and Shodhganga. However, challenges such as data privacy, security, ethical bias, copyright issues, infrastructure, costs, interoperability, and a shortage of skilled personnel remain significant concerns. This chapter highlights the need for curriculum reform in Library and Information Science (LIS), emphasising areas such as artificial intelligence knowledge, data analytics, digital curation, user experience design, computer programming fundamentals, and continuous professional development. It concludes that ethical practices, ongoing training, and collaboration among librarians, technologists, educators, and policymakers can facilitate the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence and big data, thereby enhancing teaching, learning, research, and innovation in higher education.

items.title: Next-Generation Renal Targeting Nanozymes for Acute Kidney Injury: Engineering Catalytic Therapeutics for Oxidative Stress, Immune Regulation, and Renal Repair
items.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a multifactorial clinical syndrome associated with rapid deterioration of renal function and involves interconnected processes including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, endothelial injury, programmed cell death, immune dysregulation and maladaptive repair. Current management is predominantly supportive and lacks effective pharmacological strategies that simultaneously address these pathological mechanisms. Renal-targeting nanozymes have emerged as promising catalytic nanotherapeutics that combine enzyme-mimicking activity with the tunable properties of nanomaterials. This review critically examines the engineering and therapeutic potential of renal-targeting nanozymes for AKI, focusing on nanozyme platforms, catalytic properties, renal-targeting strategies, and mechanisms underlying their antioxidant,immunomodulatory, cytoprotective, and regenerative effects. Preclinical evidence from experimental AKI models is discussed with emphasis on therapeutic outcomes, comparative performance, and current limitations. Particular attention is given to challenges involving renal accumulation, biodistribution, long-term biosafety, biodegradability,reproducibility, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory requirements. Emerging strategies, including biomimetic and biodegradable nanozymes, stimulus-responsive systems, theranostic platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted nanozyme design, are also considered. Overall, renal-targeting nanozymes represent a promising multifunctional approach for addressing the complex pathophysiology of AKI. However, standardized preclinical evaluation, scalable manufacturing, comprehensive safety assessment, appropriate regulatory frameworks, and well-designed clinical studies remain essential for translating these catalytic nanotherapeutics into clinically viable precision therapies.

items.title: Next-Generation Sacrificial Anodes for Cathodic Protection: Alloy Design, Smart Materials, Artificial Intelligence and Sustainability—A Critical Review
items.abstract: Sacrificial-anode cathodic protection remains one of the most widely applied corrosion mitigation strategies for metallic structures exposed to marine, freshwater, soil and industrial environments. Conventional zinc-, aluminum- and magnesium-based anodes have demonstrated long-standing practical value; however, increasing demands for extended service life, predictable electrochemical performance, environmental compliance and digital monitoring are reshaping the design criteria of modern cathodic protection systems. Recent research has therefore shifted from empirical alloy selection toward microstructure-controlled alloy design, smart sensing integration, data-driven prediction and sustainability-oriented material development. This critical review examines the evolution of sacrificial-anode technologies from conventional alloy systems to next-generation multifunctional anodes. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationship between alloy composition, microstructure, phase distribution, manufacturing route and electrochemical performance. The review further evaluates emerging smart sacrificial anodes incorporating embedded sensors, wireless monitoring and structural health monitoring functions, as well as the growing role of artificial intelligence, machine learning, digital twins and numerical simulation in corrosion prediction and anode lifetime assessment. Sustainability aspects, including lifecycle assessment, carbon footprint, recyclability, regulatory pressure and critical raw material dependency, are also critically discussed. This review differs from conventional alloy- or application-centered summaries by applying a four-part assessment structure: composition–processing–microstructure relationships; electrochemical and service-environment validation; sensing and data-driven lifetime management; and lifecycle sustainability. The structure is used to compare evidence maturity, identify application-specific failure modes and translate research gaps into qualification priorities. Current challenges include the lack of standardized performance datasets, limited long-term field validation, inconsistent correlation between laboratory and service environments, and insufficient integration of environmental metrics into anode design. Future research should focus on data-rich alloy development, sensor-enabled anode systems, predictive lifetime models and sustainable material selection strategies. The review concludes that next-generation sacrificial anodes will increasingly be defined not only by electrochemical efficiency, but also by intelligence, durability, environmental responsibility and system-level reliability.

items.title: Nondestructive quality and safety assessment of olive-derived products via synergistic integration of AI, big data analytics, digital twins, and computational pharmacology
items.abstract: Abstract Background Ensuring quality and safety of olive products is critical for consumer health, market value, and cultural heritage. Traditional destructive techniques are limited by their time-consuming and sample damage. Nondestructive techniques (NDT) allow real-time and non-invasive evaluation of authenticity, contamination, ripeness, and chemical composition. Artificial intelligence (AI) and big data analytics (BDA) integration enhances data interpretation, decision-making, and predictive modeling fostering transformative impact on olive industry. Aims This systematic review aimed to comprehensively evaluate advances in NDT for quality and safety assessment of olive products, emphasizing the role of AI and BDA and highlighting future prospects for industrial applications. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, from 2010 to 2026 involving spectroscopic, imaging, sensor-based methods, integrated with AI and BDA. Results NDT like near-infrared and Raman spectroscopy, ultrasound, hyperspectral and X-ray imaging, and electronic nose/tongue enable rapid and accurate assessment of chemical composition, contamination, and ripeness. When coupled with AI algorithms, they significantly improve detection sensitivity, classification accuracy, and real-time monitoring. BDA facilitate comprehensive data management, predictive modeling, and supply chain traceability. Computational pharmacology contributes to understanding complex chemical interactions and bioactive compound behavior in olive products, enhancing safety and quality assessments. Challenges include data heterogeneity, lack of standardization, high instrumentation costs, interpretability of AI models, and regulatory hurdles. Conclusion Integrating NDT with AI, BDA, and computational pharmacology offers a sustainable, efficient industrial pathway, with future research needed for standardization, portable device development, multi-sensor data fusion, and regulatory validation.

items.title: NormDetect: Anchored Calibration for Low-False-Positive Detection of Machine-Generated Web Text
items.abstract: Web platforms screen posts for text written by large language models, and every false flag hits a human writer. Detectors must therefore run at a very low false positive rate (FPR). Zero-shot detectors such as Binoculars score text with frozen language models, but invisible edits such as homoglyphs shatter tokenization and push machine text into the human range. Unicode normalization undoes these edits, yet the normalized score still misses half of the machine text at a strict FPR, under attacks that leave nothing to clean. We find that with the Falcon-7B scoring pair, heads on token statistics recall less than the normalized score at this FPR, and several flag too many human posts in some sections. We propose NormDetect, which anchors a learned per-section head to the normalized zero-shot score. A blend weight chosen on training folds under a human FPR cap combines the two scores, and one threshold is calibrated on human text only. On eight sections of the RAID benchmark with eleven attacks, NormDetect raises recall at a 0.1% calibrated FPR by 5.0 points over normalized Binoculars. Its human FPR bound stays at most 1% in every section, and no other detector within this bound recalls as much.

items.title: Nurse involvement in large language model interventions for community-dwelling older adults' health self-management: a scoping review
items.abstract: This is a retrospective registration. The searches, screening, data extraction and synthesis described here were completed before this registration was submitted; the protocol was written in advance and held by the research team but was not publicly registered at the time. We are registering now to make the protocol and the a-priori decision rules publicly auditable. Objective: to map the published evidence on large language model (LLM) interventions that support health self-management among community-dwelling older adults, and to code, for every included report, the depth of nurse involvement using a six-level nurse-in-the-loop axis. Design: scoping review reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR and conducted following JBI methodology. Two reviewers screened and extracted independently in three consecutive batches (n = 40, 40, 27); disagreements were resolved against verbatim source text. Findings were synthesised descriptively as counts, proportions, a characteristics table and an evidence map; no meta-analysis and no weighting by quality.

items.title: Nurses’ perceptions following deployment during a seismo-volcanic crisis: A qualitative study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Disaster risk is increasing globally, placing growing pressure on health systems. In geographically isolated territories, seismovolcanic crises rapidly disrupt healthcare delivery. Despite the central role of nurses in disaster response, qualitative evidence describing their experiences in isolated contexts remains limited. PURPOSE: To analyze the perceptions and experiences of nurses deployed to respond to a seismovolcanic crisis on an island without a hospital. METHODS: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted between March 2024 and November 2025. Twelve nurses involved in the response participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using interpretive qualitative content analysis supported by WebQDA software. DISCUSSION: Nurses operated under sustained uncertainty, limited situational awareness, and reliance on evacuation pathways. Their roles extended beyond clinical care to coordination, community mediation, and integration into emergency command structures. CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that clearer deployment governance, disaster-specific competency development, and recognition of nursing leadership may support preparedness and health system resilience in geographically vulnerable island settings.

items.title: Nurses' responses to patients' use of artificial intelligence for health information: a scoping review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence tools — large language model chatbots, symptom checkers, AI-based interpretation of wearable-device data, and AI-generated or AI-translated medical content — are increasingly used by patients and families to obtain health information, which they then bring into clinical encounters. This shifts part of nurses' work from providing health information toward identifying, appraising, and calibrating patient-acquired information, including correcting misinformation, addressing questions rooted in AI-generated advice, and negotiating situations where AI-derived information conflicts with professional care recommendations. Two parallel strands exist in the nursing literature: (a) internet-era research on "internet-informed patients" and nurses' responses (L___), and (b) research on nurse–clinical-AI interaction (L___). The intersection — patients' use of AI for health information and nurses' responses — has not been systematically mapped: concept boundaries are unclear, evidence is scattered, and much of it is descriptive or anecdotal. This scoping review aims to map the extent, range, and nature of evidence at this intersection, clarify concepts, describe how nurse responses are studied and measured, and identify evidence gaps to inform practice guidance, health-education strategies, and future primary research. AI-specific evidence is at an early stage; a limited number of eligible Tier 1 sources is anticipated, and a nascent-evidence finding will be reported candidly rather than compensated for by post hoc broadening of eligibility. Citation note: every factual claim in the background must carry an L number; the PMIDs listed in Section 3 are candidate sources, but full citation fields must be completed from the retrieved full texts.

items.title: Nutricoach Pro: An Agentic Real-Time Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multimodal Intelligence System for Precision Clinical Nutrition and Metabolic Health Tracking
items.abstract: Metabolic syndrome is a growing global cardiometabolic burden and is increasingly accompanied by demand for continuous, personalized, and evidence-grounded nutrition support. A 2025 systematic review and modelling analysis estimated that 1.54 billion adults were living with metabolic syndrome in 2023, with global prevalence estimated at 28.4% across women and men. Conventional nutrition trackers provide structured quantitative logging, but manual food search, portion selection, and fragmented workflows can increase interaction burden. Large language models (LLMs) provide a natural conversational interface, yet unrestricted generation can produce unsupported nutritional or clinical statements. This paper presents NutriCoach Pro, an agentic nutrition-intelligence architecture that separates deterministic computation, verified food data, evidence retrieval, multimodal perception, and language generation. The system combines a Mifflin-St Jeor energy-estimation engine, activity-adjusted energy expenditure, configurable macronutrient targets, hydration tracking, a bounded Health Compliance Score, deterministic multi-item food parsing, multimodal meal recognition, a sevendomain clinical knowledge base, local retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), optional cloud-model adapters, schema-controlled database actions, and WebSocket-based real-time synchronization. A prototype evaluation plan is defined for NLP extraction, calorieestimation error, unsupported clinical claims, latency, multimodal recognition, and user task performance. Project-reported prototype figures supplied for this manuscript are F1=96.4%, mean absolute calorie error=12.3 kcal, local-RAG latency=42.1 ms, WebSocket synchronization latency=28.4 ms, and unsupported-claim rate below 1.2%; these values are explicitly treated as provisional until reproduced with a documented held-out test protocol. The contribution is an explainable, modular, privacy-oriented architecture that places hard numerical and safety boundaries around generative Al rather than treating an LLM as the source of truth or as an autonomous Clinical decision maker

A total of 175 resident physicians who voluntarily participated were included. items.title: Occupational health hazards, knowledge and preventive practices among manual scavengers in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background: Manual scavenging continues to expose workers to serious chemical, physical, and biological hazards despite legal restrictions in India. These risks are intensified by poor protective practices and limited occupational health support. Aim was to assess occupational health hazards, knowledge, and preventive practices among manual scavengers and to examine their association with selected demographic variables. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 100 manual scavengers in Kanpur using purposive sampling. Data were collected through a structured interview schedule including self-reported occupational health hazards assessment, knowledge, and preventive practices. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation, and chi-square test. Results: Chemical, physical, and biological hazards were commonly reported. Moderate knowledge was found in 61% of participants with mean knowledge score of 15.1±3.21, while poor preventive practices were observed in 49%. Biological hazards showed a significant negative correlation with knowledge (r=−0.201, p=0.044) while knowledge and preventive practices were significantly associated with age, education, type of work, work experience, family size, and gender. Conclusions: Manual scavengers in Kanpur experience substantial occupational risk with inadequate preventive practices. Targeted occupational health education, provision of protective equipment, and policy-level support are urgently needed.

items.title: Open Digital Spaces as Emotionally Aware Learning Environments: A Collaborative Experience in TFA Programs
items.abstract: The spread of digital technologies and artificial intelligence is profoundly transforming educational processes, necessitating a shift away from an exclusively technocentric view of innovation. As Selwyn (2016) and Floridi (2014) highlight, technologies are not mere tools, but environments that influence the construction of knowledge, relationships, and professional identities. The literature highlights how emotions, trust, and a sense of belonging significantly influence participation in digital environments ( Zembylas ,2015). From this perspective, social presence (Garrison, Anderson, & Archer, 2000) and psychological safety (Edmondson, 1999) become important. This paper analyses the role of an open digital space in building an emotionally aware learning environment within the specialisation courses for support activities (TFA). The research adopts a qualitative action research approach supported by descriptive quantitative data. The study involved 1,500 students enrolled in TFA programs from different Italian regions. items.title: Open-Weight MLLMs Cannot Compare What They Cannot Name
items.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly capable of understanding images and performing complex visual reasoning, suggesting the possibility of using them to automate biological image analysis. This need is becoming increasingly urgent as advances in technology continue to generate ever larger and more diverse microscopy datasets, already exceeding the scale at which manual visual analysis is feasible. With the final aim to use MLLMs for visual comparison of complex phenotypes, we investigate a very simple baseline: comparison of the size of body parts in synthetic images of ants. We find that state-of-the-art open-weight MLLMs fail for some body parts, but not for others, even though the comparison itself is visually trivial for all of them. We evaluate different in-context learning strategies and analyze performance on the related object recognition task. Our results suggest a recognition-driven grounding failure: structures that the models cannot recognize are instead associated with a recognizable semantic concept, impairing the grounding and comparison of both. Further analysis of the vision encoder is consistent with the hypothesis that fine-grained visual structure may be less well preserved without semantic support. Together, our results reveal a surprising limitation of current MLLMs: semantic recognition can gate simple visual comparisons that do not intrinsically require semantic understanding. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/kreshuklab/Open-Weight-MLLMs-Cannot-Compare-What-They-Cannot-Name

items.title: Operationalizing CHAI: Translating Coalition for Health AI Governance Playbooks into Oracle Cloud ERP Controls
items.abstract: Healthcare organizations are enabling AI-embedded ERP features faster than governance rules are being written for them, and in mid-2026 the rules arrived faster than most solution architects expected. The Coalition for Health AI published eight governance playbooks on 27 May 2026, and five days later the Joint Commission opened its voluntary Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare certification, which means a surveyor can now ask a health system to demonstrate its AI governance rather than describe it. Neither document specifies which system setting enforces any of it, and arguably neither should, since both are written to apply across every vendor a health system might run. This paper closes that gap for one platform. Six governance domains running through the CHAI playbooks and RUAIH guidance, namely accountability, transparency, human oversight, pre-deployment risk assessment, continuous monitoring, and third-party risk, are each mapped to a control that already exists inside Oracle Cloud ERP: role-based security profiles, approval hierarchies, and the execution traceability introduced with Oracle's 2026 Fusion Agentic Applications and AI Agent Studio. The mapping is supported by a four-tier risk model that determines how much autonomy an agent may hold, an audit evidence model stating what a surveyor should be shown for each domain, and a six-step implementation sequence. The contribution is a practitioner synthesis drawn from Oracle Cloud ERP transformation programs in regulated health systems. It is not a controlled study, and no compliance outcome, audit finding rate, or certification result is reported or claimed.

items.title: Opinion Mining for Product Reviews Using Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce platforms has resulted in a large volume of customer-generated product reviews. These reviews contain valuable information about customer opinions, satisfaction levels, product quality, and specific product features. However, manually analysing a large number of reviews is time-consuming and difficult. Opinion mining, also known as sentiment analysis, uses Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing techniques to automatically identify and classify opinions expressed in textual reviews. This paper presents a conceptual AI-based framework for analysing product reviews and identifying their sentiment polarity as positive, negative, or neutral. The proposed approach combines contextual language representation using Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) with aspect-based sentiment analysis inspired by Aspect-specific Graph Convolutional Networks (ASGCN). The system performs review preprocessing, contextual feature extraction, aspect identification, sentiment classification, and generation of an overall opinion summary. The reviewed literature also includes hybrid BERT-CNN architectures, user/context-aware graph modelling, and multimodal learning approaches, which provide additional directions for improving opinion analysis. The proposed framework aims to provide more detailed and meaningful information than simple positive or negative classification by identifying the product aspects responsible for customer opinions. items.title: Opportunities and risks of AI in lesson planning: insights from pre-service teachers
items.abstract: This contribution presents an exploratory study on pre-service teachers' perceptions of the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in lesson planning, with a focus on opportunities, risks, and conditions for effective integration into instructional design. The study is grounded in the TPACK framework (Mishra & Koehler, 2006) and its extension Intelligent-TPACK (Celik, 2023), which incorporates an explicit ethical dimension into teachers' technological and pedagogical knowledge. Within this perspective, AI tools such as chatbots, intelligent tutoring systems, and automated planning systems are not neutral instruments but sociotechnical systems that require critical evaluation in terms of transparency, fairness, and accountability. The theoretical approach adopted here is further informed by critical AI literacy perspectives, which emphasise the need for teachers to develop not only operational competence but also the ability to interrogate the assumptions and biases embedded in algorithmic outputs. items.title: Optimalisasi Bimbingan Belajar Bahasa Arab Berbasis Nilai-Nilai Akhlak sebagai Upaya Pencegahan Putus Sekolah di Daerah Terpencil
items.abstract: This study aims to examine the effectiveness of the Arabic language tutoring program (bimbingan belajar Bahasa Arab) at SMK Negeri 1 Mesuji, Ogan Komering Ilir Regency, where the dropout rate reaches 17.3%, and to formulate an optimization model for that program grounded in Pendidikan Akidah Akhlak (Islamic Creed and Morals Education) to build students' character and resilience and to prevent dropout. This explanatory sequential mixed-methods study used primary data from students, teachers, and parents. Of the students actively participating in the Arabic language tutoring program, 50 respondents were selected through stratified random sampling (Slovin formula) to complete a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire, which was analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS 26. Qualitative data were collected through in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, and participant observation with key informants selected through purposive sampling, and were analyzed thematically using NVivo 12. Quantitative results show that the effectiveness of the Arabic language tutoring was mostly in the moderate category (76%) and did not significantly affect Akidah Akhlak-based resilience (t = 0.340; sig = 0.735), whereas intrinsic motivation did (t = 2.587; sig = 0.013; R² = 0.400). Qualitative findings show that informants regard the Arabic tutoring as helpful for understanding the material yet still academically oriented, that spiritual resilience is students' primary coping mechanism against external constraints, and that all informants expect an Arabic language tutoring model that integrates Akidah Akhlak. The study proposes an optimization model for Arabic language tutoring built on five strategies: integrating Akidah Akhlak values into Arabic tutoring materials, strengthening intrinsic motivation and character, adopting a holistic learning approach, fostering school–teacher–parent collaboration, and providing continuous mentoring for students at risk of dropping out.

items.title: Orchestrating Big Data and Artificial Intelligence for Adaptive Digital Business Strategy
items.abstract: The rapid acceleration of digital transformation has changed the way organizations formulate and implement business strategies, requiring firms to become more adaptive, data-driven, and responsive to dynamic market conditions. This study aims to examine how big data and artificial intelligence can be orchestrated as integrated strategic capabilities to support adaptive digital business strategy. Using a qualitative conceptual approach, this study applies a structured literature review and thematic synthesis to analyze previous studies related to big data capability, artificial intelligence capability, governance mechanisms, intelligent business insight, and strategic adaptability. The results show that big data functions as a strategic foundation by providing diverse information from customers, markets, operations, and digital platforms, while artificial intelligence acts as an intelligent decision engine that transforms data into predictions, recommendations, automation, and actionable business insights. The findings also indicate that governance and human decision-making are essential in ensuring that the use of big data and AI remains reliable, transparent, accountable, secure, and aligned with organizational objectives. This study concludes that adaptive digital business strategy emerges from the continuous orchestration of data resources, AI systems, governance structures, human judgment, and strategic execution. The proposed framework contributes to digital business literature by explaining how AI-driven big data orchestration can improve decision quality, agility, competitiveness, innovation, operational efficiency, and sustainable digital value creation. In addition, the discussion is expanded to include cybersecurity, data privacy, secure data processing, and AI risk management as critical enablers of large-scale data-driven business systems.

items.title: Organisational Development and Industrial Democracy
items.abstract: This chapter provides an overview of Eric Miller’s contribution to organizational development and industrial democracy, situating his practice within the Tavistock tradition that integrates open systems thinking, socio-technical systems (STS) design, and psychoanalytic perspectives on group and organizational life. Miller argued that organizations are not merely rational structures, but emotional and social systems in which anxiety, defence, and unconscious processes shape behaviour, decision-making, and capacity for change. Central to his approach is the concept of the organization as an open system whose viability depends on effective boundary management, between sub-systems, levels of authority, and the organization and its environment. Building on STS principles, Miller emphasized joint optimization: designing technical processes and social arrangements in tandem so that task requirements and human needs are aligned. He extended this work by making visible the defensive patterns that emerge under stress, splitting, projection, denial, scapegoating, and rigidity, and by showing how authority and leadership often become focal points for organizational anxieties. His consultancy therefore combined structural diagnosis with reflective inquiry into role, power, and emotional experience. The chapter illustrates these themes through emblematic cases: the coal mining studies that shaped STS foundations; applications in healthcare where hierarchy and communication can become defensive; work with the Church of England on identity and authority in a changing environment; and the Norwegian Industrial Democracy Project, demonstrating how participative work design can enhance resilience and performance. Overall, this part frames Miller’s legacy as a disciplined, practice-oriented synthesis of system and psyche, offering enduring concepts for contemporary organizational change.

items.title: Organizational mechanisms in digital public health transformation: change communication, collective sensemaking, and cross-functional collaboration
items.abstract: Introduction Digital public health transformation extends beyond technology deployment and requires organizational processes that align interpretation, coordination, governance, and population-health goals. Existing research examines change communication, collective sensemaking, and cross-functional collaboration separately, with limited integration of their boundaries, recursive interactions, cross-level transmission, and multilevel outcomes. This review develops an organizational explanation of how these mechanisms may support transformation. Methods A narrative integrative review synthesized theoretical, empirical, policy, and technical literature from organizational science, implementation science, digital public health, data governance, and artificial intelligence governance. Searches covered PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, APA PsycINFO, CINAHL, IEEE Xplore, ProQuest Public Health Database, Business Source Complete, and traceable institutional sources from inception to October 1, 2026. Sources were purposively selected for relevance, contribution, public health applicability, analytical level, and traceability. Synthesis used construct coding, within-theme comparison, framework comparison, cross-level mechanism mapping, and analysis of competing explanations and evidence boundaries. Results Change communication establishes credible and contestable direction; collective sensemaking develops shared problem representations; cross-functional collaboration translates shared understanding into coordinated action. They operate recursively rather than sequentially. A seven-layer framework links structural contextual conditions, organizational mechanisms, potential mediating capabilities, implementation outcomes, organizational or system outcomes, population-level service and equity outcomes, and population health outcomes. Team psychological safety moderates the relationship between proximal support conditions and risk-detection behaviors, which feed back into the mechanisms. Organizational readiness for change, knowledge absorption and translation, interoperability governance, organizational learning, and resilience are proposed as mediating capabilities. Power and equity governance, community decision rights, representativeness, vendor accountability, auditing, appeals, portability, and exit management cut across the framework. The model complements CFIR, NASSS, i-PARIHS, EPIS, and sociotechnical approaches by specifying observable interactive mechanisms and feedback pathways. Discussion The framework provides a testable explanatory structure and governance-diagnostic tool for surveillance, data infrastructures, laboratory networks, artificial intelligence, and community co-production. Evidence more strongly supports organizational and system processes than causal effects on population health. Longitudinal, multilevel, and mechanism-oriented studies should test mediation, moderation, feedback, equity, and cross-level transmission.

items.title: Overtrust in Generative AI and Students’ Critical Thinking: An Integrated PLS-SEM and Machine Learning Analysis in Vietnamese Higher Education
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative AI (GenAI) among university students has raised concerns that excessive trust in AI outputs may erode critical thinking. This study examines how overtrust relates to critical thinking through cognitive offloading and AI dependency, with AI literacy as a protective moderator, integrating partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with machine learning. Survey data from 580 Vietnamese undergraduates were analysed through a five-step pipeline: exploratory structure learning, confirmatory path estimation, predictive benchmarking, explainable AI, and heterogeneous-effect estimation. Overtrust was associated with higher offloading (β = 0.390) and dependency (β = 0.402), both of which were associated with lower critical thinking (β = -0.251 and -0.348), while AI literacy buffered the association with dependency (interaction β = 0.154). Crucially, the direct effect of overtrust was non-significant and the two mediators carried 89% of its total effect, indicating indirect-only mediation. A parsimonious six-variable classifier separated at-risk students with AUC ≈ 0.77, whereas demographics alone performed at chance; SHAP analysis identified AI dependency as the dominant feature in the classification decision, and a causal forest confirmed the buffering pattern across the low-to-mid range while exposing a non-monotonic reversal under sparse support at the upper tail. Interventions should therefore target AI-use behaviour rather than trust itself. These findings are associational rather than causal: the design is cross-sectional with all measures self-reported at a single point, so the classifier performs concurrent screening rather than temporal prediction.

items.title: Pedagogy and teaching in emergency contexts in the age Of artificial intelligence: towards a human-centred Framework for educational continuity, inclusion and Resilience
items.abstract: The contemporary global educational landscape is increasingly vulnerable to systemic crises, including natural disasters, public health emergencies, armed conflicts, and socioeconomic instability. These events do not merely interrupt educational continuity; they exacerbate existing social, economic, and geographic inequalities, disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations (Burde et al., 2017). In this context, Education in Emergencies (EiE) must be understood not only as a temporary humanitarian response, but as a structural and pedagogical imperative for safeguarding the universal right to education. Educational resilience therefore requires a shift from reactive and fragmented models toward proactive and adaptive systems capable of anticipating, absorbing, and recovering from crises without compromising the quality and equity of teaching and learning. This resilience cannot be achieved without integrating the psychological, emotional, and relational dimensions of education. Trauma-informed education highlights how large-scale crises can profoundly affect students, families, and teachers, altering stress regulation and compromising cognitive, executive, and socio-relational functioning essential to learning (Avery et al., 2021; Berger, 2024).
